sourceEvidence.claim: KimiOAuthToolkit defaults credential storage to its homeDir/credentials
Refresh lock is per configDir/oauth/provider; isolated homes do not share a refresh lock
Refresh reads isolated storage, saves refreshed tokens there, unauthorized saves revoked tombstone
Credential JSON is atomically saved under selected storage directory

copyImplementation.behavior: Both read controller Path.home()/.kimi-code; copy credentials and oauth with copy2 metadata; child HOME and KIMI_CODE_HOME isolated. No back-propagation of refreshed credential state.

findings: Generated P141/P142 config bytes match. No evidence of omitted credential file or wrong configured source.
P142 unlaunched terminal credential bytes equal current original source; source mtime remains 03:57 UTC.
P141 native and terminal credentials changed in isolated homes at 11:08/11:09 UTC and both access/refresh hashes differ from the unchanged source.
P142 native first use rejected its authorization grant and wrote an empty-token revoked tombstone to its isolated home, consistent with installed refresh failure path.
Copying refreshable credentials into independent homes creates divergent token/lock histories. Recopying the unchanged original source later can select stale refresh material.
conclusion: Strong evidence of a harness credential-lineage hazard, not evidence that the user account itself is broken. P142 copied the intended original file but that file had not received P141 isolated refresh updates. Provider-side exact revocation/rotation policy and causal attribution cannot be proven from local evidence alone.
limits: Source-account authentication was not tested and is neither proven valid nor invalid.
P141 isolated refreshed tokens are also time-limited and were not reused or refreshed for this diagnosis.
No fake-auth reproduction or harness behavior change performed: exact real provider refresh policy is not known, and a simulation would not establish that policy.
P142 unknown usage/cost and failed-batch verdict remain unchanged.
nextSafeDesign: Before any separately approved retry, define a single controlled credential refresh lineage using a CLI-supported account/storage interface while retaining session/memory isolation; or stop preflight on an expired copied snapshot. Do not silently copy isolated refreshed credentials back to global storage, invent a token source, or infer auth validity from presence/expiry alone.
